name: spec.json
description: The normative source. Every value the spec sets, with units. Where an implementation and this file disagree, this file is right.
lede: The normative source. Every value the spec sets, with units. Where an implementation and this file disagree, this file is right.

name: typeset.css
description: The CSS implementation. Everything is scoped to .typeset, so it cannot leak into surrounding markup. Drop it in and add the class.
lede: The CSS implementation. Everything is scoped to .typeset, so it cannot leak into surrounding markup. Drop it in and add the class.
extra: Fonts are not included. The page must load EB Garamond, Source Sans 3 and IBM Plex Mono itself. For a document you send, self-host and embed them rather than fetching from a CDN at print time — and note that Google's build of EB Garamond has no real small caps, so the browser synthesises them. Browse the font files →

name: typeset.typ
description: The Typst implementation. Same specification, different engine — and Typst does the things CSS cannot: page-foot footnotes, running heads, and table-of-contents page numbers, all natively.
lede: The Typst implementation. Same specification, different engine — and Typst does the things CSS cannot: page-foot footnotes, running heads, and table-of-contents page numbers, all natively.
extra:
Typst needs the font files themselves. Unlike CSS there is no URL to point at: a font is either in the project or it is not, and a missing family is substituted silently. So this one ships as a bundle — the implementation, all three example documents, and the three font families the spec names, licences included.

Compile with typst compile --font-path fonts implementations/example-essay.typ out.pdf, or drag the unzipped folder into a typst.app project.

The bundle is built from this repository on every deploy, so it can never drift from the fonts and implementation above.

name: iawriter.css
description: The iA Writer layer. iA Writer is Markdown only, so the template gets headings, body text, bold, italic, tables, footnotes and one quote — and this file maps that vocabulary onto typeset.css.
lede: The iA Writer layer. iA Writer is Markdown only, so a template gets headings, body text, bold, italic, tables, footnotes and one quoting construct and nothing else — and this file is what maps that vocabulary onto typeset.css. It adds no typography of its own; the page, and anything the letter wants for itself, live in letter/page.css.
extra:
One template: the letter. Ragged right at the 11pt base, filling an A4 page with 20mm margins, with a display quote and a letterhead of its own — the level-1 heading is the name, and an indented block, stripped of every mark of code, is the address.

It ships as a bundle carrying typeset.css and every font face it binds, because a template is a local page with no network and WebKit substitutes a missing face without saying so. Built from this repository on every deploy, so it cannot drift from the stylesheet above.

There is no two-column iA Writer template. WebKit honours every CSS multi-column property on screen and ignores all of them when printing, so such a template previews in two columns and exports in one, with nothing to say it changed. Two columns belong to an engine that can paginate them: Typst does it natively.

No running head and no folio. iA Writer reserves those bands by setting the page margins itself, so a band and a @page margin cannot both be declared — and the page is the thing worth having.
